questions.question_html: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y^{2}=x^{3}$ , the $y$ -axis and the lines $y=1$ and $y=8$ is

options.label: A
options.html: $\frac{155}{3}$ sq. units

options.label: B
options.html: $\frac{93}{5}$ sq. units

options.label: C
options.html: $93$ sq. units

options.label: D
options.html: $155$ sq. units

questions.explanation_text: The curve is $y^{2}=x^{3}$ Since the region is between the lines $y=1$ and $y=8$ , it is easier to write $x$ in terms of $y$ . From $y^{2}=x^{3}$ we get $x=y^{2/3}$ The $y$ -axis is $x=0$ . So, for each value of $y$ from $1$ to $8$ , the horizontal width of the region is $x_{\text{right}}-x_{\text{left}}=y^{2/3}-0=y^{2/3}$ Hence, the required area is $\int_{1}^{8}y^{2/3}dy$ Now, $\int y^{2/3}dy=\frac{y^{5/3}}{5/3}=\frac{3}{5}y^{5/3}$ So, $\text{Area}=[\frac{3}{5}y^{5/3}]_{1}^{8}$ $=\frac{3}{5}(8^{5/3}-1^{5/3})$ Since $8^{1/3}=2$ we have $8^{5/3}=2^{5}=32$ Thus, $\text{Area}=\frac{3}{5}(32-1)$ $=\frac{3}{5} \times 31$ $=\frac{93}{5}$ So, the area is $\frac{93}{5}\text{sq. units}$ Correct option: Option B .
questions.explanation_html:
The curve is

$y^{2}=x^{3}$

Since the region is between the lines $y=1$ and $y=8$ , it is easier to write $x$ in terms of $y$ .

From

$y^{2}=x^{3}$

we get

$x=y^{2/3}$

The $y$ -axis is $x=0$ .

So, for each value of $y$ from $1$ to $8$ , the horizontal width of the region is

$x_{\text{right}}-x_{\text{left}}=y^{2/3}-0=y^{2/3}$

Hence, the required area is

$\int_{1}^{8}y^{2/3}dy$

Now,

$\int y^{2/3}dy=\frac{y^{5/3}}{5/3}=\frac{3}{5}y^{5/3}$

So,

$\text{Area}=[\frac{3}{5}y^{5/3}]_{1}^{8}$

$=\frac{3}{5}(8^{5/3}-1^{5/3})$

Since

$8^{1/3}=2$

we have

$8^{5/3}=2^{5}=32$

Thus,

$\text{Area}=\frac{3}{5}(32-1)$

$=\frac{3}{5} \times 31$

$=\frac{93}{5}$

So, the area is

$\frac{93}{5}\text{sq. units}$

Correct option: Option B.

questions.explanation_text: The required area is found by integrating the function $y=sin(\frac{x}{3})$ from $x=0$ to $x=3\pi$ . This gives the definite integral: $\int_{0}^{3\pi}sin(\frac{x}{3})dx$ To integrate $sin(\frac{x}{3})$ , we use substitution. The integral becomes $-3cos(\frac{x}{3})$ . Now substitute the limits $0$ and $3\pi$ : $\begin{aligned} & \int_{0}^{3\pi}sin(\frac{x}{3})dx \\ & (-3 \cdot cos\frac{x}{3})_{0}^{3\pi}=(-3(-1))-(-3(1))=6 \end{aligned}$ So, the total area is $6$ .

$\begin{aligned} & \int_{0}^{3\pi}sin(\frac{x}{3})dx \\ & (-3 \cdot cos\frac{x}{3})_{0}^{3\pi}=(-3(-1))-(-3(1))=6 \end{aligned}$

questions.explanation_text: Given equation of curve, $y^{2}=8x\text{and line}y=2x$ Now, intersecting points of given curve and line. $\begin{aligned} & & (2x)^{2} & =8x \\ \Rightarrow & 4x^{2} & =8x \\ \Rightarrow & & x & =0,2 \end{aligned}$ Putting values of $x$ in $y=2x$ then, we get $y=0,4$ $\therefore$ Required area of bounded region. $\begin{aligned} & =\int_{0}^{2}(\sqrt{8x}-2x)dx \\ & =\int_{0}^{2}(2\sqrt{2} \cdot x^{1/2}-2x)dx \\ & =2\int_{0}^{2}(\sqrt{2} \cdot x^{1/2}-x)dx \\ & =2[\sqrt{2}\int_{0}^{2}x^{1/2}dx-\int_{0}^{2}xdx] \end{aligned}$ $\begin{aligned} & =2[\sqrt{2}(\frac{x^{3/2}}{3/2})_{0}^{2}-(\frac{x^{2}}{2})_{0}^{2}] \\ & =2[\sqrt{2} \cdot \frac{2}{3}(2)^{3/2}-2] \\ & =2[\frac{8}{3}-2]=2(\frac{2}{3})=\frac{4}{3}\text{sq. units} \end{aligned}$
questions.explanation_html:
Given equation of curve,

$y^{2}=8x\text{and line}y=2x$

Now, intersecting points of given curve and line.

$\begin{aligned} & & (2x)^{2} & =8x \\ \Rightarrow & 4x^{2} & =8x \\ \Rightarrow & & x & =0,2 \end{aligned}$

Putting values of $x$ in $y=2x$ then, we get $y=0,4$

$\therefore$ Required area of bounded region.

$\begin{aligned} & =\int_{0}^{2}(\sqrt{8x}-2x)dx \\ & =\int_{0}^{2}(2\sqrt{2} \cdot x^{1/2}-2x)dx \\ & =2\int_{0}^{2}(\sqrt{2} \cdot x^{1/2}-x)dx \\ & =2[\sqrt{2}\int_{0}^{2}x^{1/2}dx-\int_{0}^{2}xdx] \end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned} & =2[\sqrt{2}(\frac{x^{3/2}}{3/2})_{0}^{2}-(\frac{x^{2}}{2})_{0}^{2}] \\ & =2[\sqrt{2} \cdot \frac{2}{3}(2)^{3/2}-2] \\ & =2[\frac{8}{3}-2]=2(\frac{2}{3})=\frac{4}{3}\text{sq. units} \end{aligned}$

questions.question_html: The area bounded by the line $y=x,X$ -axis and ordinates $x=-1$ and $x=2$ is

options.label: A
options.html: $\frac{3}{2}$

options.label: B
options.html: $\frac{5}{2}$

options.label: C
options.html: 2

options.label: D
options.html: 3

questions.explanation_text: Given line is $y=x,X$ -axis, $x=-1$ and $x=2$ $\begin{aligned} \text{Required area} & =|\int_{-1}^{0}xdx|+\int_{0}^{2}xdx \\ & =|[\frac{x^{2}}{2}]_{-1}^{0}|+[\frac{x^{2}}{2}]_{0}^{2} \\ & =|(0-\frac{1}{2})|+(2-0) \\ & =\frac{1}{2}+2=\frac{5}{2}\text{sq units} \end{aligned}$
questions.explanation_html:

questions.question_text: Area of the region bounded by the curve $y=cosx,x=0$ and $x=\pi$ is
questions.question_html: Area of the region bounded by the curve $y=cosx,x=0$ and $x=\pi$ is

options.label: A
options.html: 4 sq units

options.label: B
options.html: 3 sq units

options.label: C
options.html: 1 sq units

options.label: D
options.html: 2 sq units

questions.explanation_html: $\begin{aligned} RequiredArea & =\int_{0}^{\pi}|cosx|dx \\ & =2\int_{0}^{\pi/2}|cosx|dx \\ & =2\int_{0}^{\pi/2}cosxdx \\ & =2[sinx]_{0}^{\pi/2} \\ & =2[sin\frac{\pi}{2}-sin0] \\ & =2(1-0) \\ & =2\text{sq units.} \end{aligned}$

questions.question_text: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y=x^{2}$ and the line $y=16$
questions.question_html: The area of the region bounded by the curve $y=x^{2}$ and the line $y=16$

options.label: A
options.html: $\frac{64}{3}$ sq units

options.label: B
options.html: $\frac{32}{3}sq$ units

options.label: C
options.html: $\frac{256}{3}$ sq units

options.label: D
options.html: $\frac{128}{3}$ sq units

questions.explanation_html:
$\text{According to the question,}$

$\begin{aligned} \text{Required area} & =2\int_{0}^{16}xdy \\ & =2\int_{0}^{16}\sqrt{y}dy \\ & =2[\frac{y^{3/2}}{3/2}]_{0}^{16} \\ & =\frac{4}{3}[16^{3/2}-0^{3/2}] \\ & =\frac{4}{3} \times 64=\frac{256}{3}\text{sq units.} \end{aligned}$
